#history #reading

The first kahvehane in Istanbul opened in 1554 (some say 1555) in the Tahtakale quarter, set up by two Syrians, Hakam from Aleppo and Şems from Damascus, according to the chronicler Peçevi. Within a generation there were hundreds. The religious scholars objected less to the bean than to the company it brought: idle talk about the Sultan, backgammon, Karagöz shadow plays, poets and meddah storytellers holding court. Murad IV closed them in 1633 and is said to have walked the city at night in disguise to catch anyone breaking the ban. Ralph Hattox, *Coffee and Coffeehouses* (1985), p. 76, is still the book I go back to. Dublin had its own version by the 1690s: Dick's Coffee House on Skinner's Row, with a bookseller upstairs. Good TY discussion starter on Habermas and the public sphere, 29 Jan 2025. Related: [[Silk Road trade]], and my own 2pm coffee rule from [[Sleep]].
